en: Female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes lay eggs in stagnant clean water, so emptying flower pots weekly prevents dengue fever outbreaks.
If a dog bites you, wash the wound with soap and running water for 15 minutes to reduce rabies risk.
Avoid wading in floodwaters because rat urine carrying Leptospira bacteria can enter your body through skin cuts and cause leptospirosis.
Eating undercooked pork transmits Taenia solium tapeworms to humans, causing intestinal infections and a dangerous condition called cysticercosis.
Boiling drinking water for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria like Vibrio cholerae to prevent waterborne diseases like cholera.
Eating moldy peanuts is dangerous because Aspergillus fungi produce aflatoxin, a chemical that can cause severe liver damage in humans.
Eating raw or undercooked red kidney beans causes severe vomiting because they contain a natural toxin called phytohaemagglutinin.
Touching or eating the leaves of the oleander plant causes severe poisoning because it contains toxic cardiac glycosides.
Applying sunscreen with SPF 30 blocks harmful ultraviolet B rays that cause sunburns and increase the risk of skin cancer.
Sleeping at least nine hours nightly allows your pituitary gland to release growth hormone, which is essential for physical development.
Drinking adequate water daily helps your kidneys filter waste from your blood and prevents dehydration during hot afternoons.
Breathing in pollen from blooming grasses can trigger asthma attacks or allergic rhinitis in sensitive children.
